name: Lunar south polar highlands (pole-centred region containing Artemis III candidate regions)
illumination_summary: Peaks along the rim of Shackleton are illuminated about 80–90% of each lunar orbit (literature); PSRs never illuminated
ice_evidence: Cold traps >80° latitude host most water-ice cold-trap area (Hayne et al. 2021 summarised in wiki:Lunar water).
hazards: steep crater walls and massif slopes; long low-angle shadows; extreme thermal gradients between sunlit and shadowed terrain; no atmosphere; radiation; 1/6 g
mission_objectives: crewed landing (Artemis III candidate regions); polar volatiles prospecting; sample of ancient crust; power from near-continuous illumination

name: Shackleton crater and rim vicinity
illumination_summary: rim peaks ~80–90% illuminated; interior in perpetual darkness
ice_evidence: LOLA reflectance analysis suggests up to 22% of Shackleton's surface may be covered in ice (wiki:Lunar water; Zuber et al. 2012).
hazards: ~4.2 km deep conical crater with steep walls; permanent shadow in interior; thermal extremes
mission_objectives: PSR volatiles access; illuminated rim for power; ancient crust sampling

name: Malapert massif
illumination_summary: two ridge regions illuminated ~74% of the lunar year (Bussey et al. 2010 as cited by Allender et al. 2019)
ice_evidence: Small-scale PSRs in surrounding area (Allender et al. 2019).
hazards: massif rises ~5 km; slopes 15–25° on ridge approaches (Allender et al. 2019)
mission_objectives: Artemis III candidate region; Earth line-of-sight communications; SPA basin rim material

name: Cabeus crater permanently shadowed region (LCROSS impact target)
illumination_summary: main crater lit ~25% of lunar day; western part in permanent shadow
ice_evidence: LCROSS ejecta water concentration 5.6 ± 2.9% by mass (Colaprete et al. 2010, as reported in wiki:Lunar water).
hazards: permanent darkness; <100 K surfaces; crater walls

name: Marius Hills pit (mare volcanic dome field)
dem_product: LRO LOLA global LDEM 118 m (USGS Astrogeology mosaic, Mar 2014)
illumination_summary: pit floor partly overhung (LROC Pits Atlas: Overhang=Y)
hazards: ~40 m deep pit (LROC atlas); boulder-covered floor; overhangs
mission_objectives: lava-tube / subsurface habitat scouting; radiation and thermal shelter

name: Mare Tranquillitatis pit
dem_product: LRO LOLA global LDEM 118 m (USGS Astrogeology mosaic, Mar 2014)
illumination_summary: pit floor partly in permanent shadow beneath overhang
hazards: ~100 m deep pit (NASA 2022 release); vertical walls; illuminated floor >420 K peak (modeled)
mission_objectives: lava-tube / subsurface habitat scouting; thermal-stable shelter

name: Apollo 11 Tranquility Base (mare regolith plains)
dem_product: LRO LOLA global LDEM 118 m (USGS Astrogeology mosaic, Mar 2014)
illumination_summary: equatorial day/night cycle (~29.5 Earth days synodic)
hazards: regolith dust; small craters and boulders
mission_objectives: mare regolith handling; surface mobility on plains

name: Jezero crater delta (Perseverance landing site)
dem_product: MGS MOLA global DEM 463 m (USGS Astrogeology mosaic)
mission_objectives: astrobiology/biosignatures in lacustrine sediments; sample caching for return

name: Gale crater (Curiosity Bradbury Landing)
dem_product: MGS MOLA global DEM 463 m (USGS Astrogeology mosaic)
hazards: sharp rocks (wheel damage reported in mission literature, not quantified here); dunes
mission_objectives: habitability of ancient lakes; stratigraphy of Aeolis Mons

name: Elysium Planitia volcanic plains (InSight landing site)
dem_product: MGS MOLA global DEM 463 m (USGS Astrogeology mosaic)
ice_evidence: Possible ash-covered water ice reported near 5°N 150°E (Mars Express, wiki:Elysium Planitia) - debated.
hazards: low hazards; selected as smooth, flat plains
mission_objectives: geophysics; safe landing on flat plains; habitat siting on low-slope terrain

name: Vastitas Borealis periglacial plains (Phoenix landing site)
dem_product: MGS MOLA global DEM 463 m (USGS Astrogeology mosaic)
mission_objectives: ice-soil boundary habitability; ISRU ground ice

name: Planum Boreum north polar layered deposits
dem_product: MGS MOLA global DEM 463 m (USGS Astrogeology mosaic)
ice_evidence: Ice cap mostly water ice (~95%) with dust layers (wiki:Planum Boreum).
hazards: scarps up to ~2 km; avalanches off scarps (HiRISE); polar night

name: Arsia Mons flank cave skylights (lava tubes / basaltic shield)
dem_product: MGS MOLA global DEM 463 m (USGS Astrogeology mosaic)
ice_evidence: Orographic water-ice cloud (atmospheric), not ground ice.
hazards: high elevation, thin atmosphere for EDL; pit walls

name: Arcadia Planitia mid-latitude ground ice plains
dem_product: MGS MOLA global DEM 463 m (USGS Astrogeology mosaic)
ice_evidence: Excess ice widespread in mid-latitudes, especially Arcadia Planitia (wiki).
mission_objectives: ISRU ground ice for human missions; low-elevation EDL
